title: Using AliasedClass in model module causes NameError/InvalidRequestError
body:
I have relationship that requires a complex join and have used this [non-primary mapper approach](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/12/orm/join_conditions.html#relationship-to-non-primary-mapper) in the past to achieve it.  Since the `non_primary` mapper setting is deprecated in `1.3` I'm attempting to migrate to using an `AliasedClass` per this [guide](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/changelog/migration_13.html#relationship-to-aliasedclass-replaces-the-need-for-non-primary-mappers).  However creating an instance of AliasedClass in any of the files that contain models is causing an error to be thrown, I believe, when the declarative base is loaded. Python: 2.7 & 3.6
SQLAlchemy: 1.3.3

The ORM my company uses is quite large and the basic structure is this:  All model classes extend a single declarative base and there is a package for each database schema and a module for each model.  Imports are used in package `__init__.py` files to import all models to the top level package which is where the declarative base is defined.  Here is a basic example of what will cause this error when the base is imported (which triggers the loading of all of the model classes):

```py

class VehicleInfo(Base):
    __tablename__ = 'vehicle_info'

...

vehicle_info_alias = aliased(VehicleInfo)
```

Thanks in advance if you get a chance to take a look at this and am glad to provide any more info that is needed.
